artists.biography: Ride were a British shoegazing band that formed in 1988 in Oxford, England, consisting of Andy Bell, Mark Gardener, Laurence "Loz" Colbert, and Steve Queralt. The band were initially part of the "shoegazing" scene that emerged in England during the early 1990s. Following the break-up of the band in 1996, members moved on to various other projects, most notably Bell who became the bassist for Oasis. In 2001, the band members were briefly reunited for a one-off performance for a television show. Their debut album 'Nowhere' has been named one of the greatest albums of the shoegazing genre, Nowhere was voted number 74 on Pitchfork Media's list of the Top 100 Albums of the 1990s, and closing track "Vapour Trail" was voted at number 145 on Pitchfork's Top 200 Tracks of the 90s. The album is also included in the book '1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die'.

perplexity.description:
4 EPs" by Ride, originally released in 2022, compiles the band's first four EPs—Ride, Play, Fall, and Today Forever—onto a single collection for the first time. These recordings, originally issued between 1989 and 1990, capture Ride at the outset of their career, showcasing their signature blend of shoegaze and alternative rock. The album features swirling guitar textures, driving rhythms, and ethereal melodies, with tracks like "Chelsea Girl," "Drive Blind," "Like a Daydream," and "Seagull" exemplifying the band's early sound and influence on the genre.

Musically, "4 EPs" stands as a foundational document in Ride's discography, bridging their raw debut singles with the expansive sound of their later albums. The collection highlights the band's ability to merge melodic songwriting with atmospheric production, a hallmark of the shoegaze movement. Released by Wichita Recordings, the album was well-received for its historical significance and sonic cohesion, praised by critics for presenting Ride's formative work in a comprehensive and accessible format.
